{{nihongo|'''Ibe Iwakura Shrine'''|飯部磐座神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echizen Province]].

It is listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=minor Shikinaisha}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. Within the shrine grounds, artificially made iwakura stones transported from elsewhere are piled up.

=== History ===
A fire broke out in {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}} 11 ({{ill|1726|Q6936|qid=Q6936}}), and old records were lost. According to the information board on the shrine grounds, in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 15 ({{ill|873|Q30369|qid=Q30369}}), a local powerful family, the Ibe no Miyatsuko Toyomochi clan, transported and stacked large rocks to create an iwakura, built a shrine hall, and founded the shrine. It is said that clan iwakura rituals were conducted there.<ref>Information board within the grounds of Ibei Iwakura Shrine.</ref>
;Main hall
:Built in {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 6 ({{ill|1823|Q6988|qid=Q6988}}) August<ref name="yoshino">{{Cite book|Japanese|year=|title=50th Anniversary Commemorative Book of Yoshino District’s Incorporation into the City “Yoshino”|editor=|page={{Page number needed|date=February 2017}}}}</ref>. Repaired in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 3 ({{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}}).
;Worship hall
:Built in Taishō 4 ({{ill|1915|Q2084|qid=Q2084}}) July.
;Corridor
